question: Should OpenClaw add a new model-facing parent-only sub-agent send contract, and should it be a dedicated `sessions_send_parent` tool or a reserved `sessionKey: "parent"` target?
rationale: The implementation changes session authorization boundaries and model-facing tool semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Add a dedicated parent-only contract
options.body: Implement a dedicated tool or trusted parent selector that derives the direct parent from spawn metadata and rejects siblings, ancestors, cross-agent targets, stale parents, and automatic forwarding.

options.title: Defer to completion handoff work
options.body: Keep mid-run child-to-parent sends unsupported and focus only on completion announce/session-yield orchestration.

options.title: Use broad opt-in sessions_send
options.body: Document the existing broader allowlist/visibility configuration path, accepting the larger authorization surface for trusted operators.

recommendation.title: Add a dedicated parent-only contract
recommendation.body: Implement a dedicated tool or trusted parent selector that derives the direct parent from spawn metadata and rejects siblings, ancestors, cross-agent targets, stale parents, and automatic forwarding.
